items.text: **A volume gauge beside the speaker.** A half ring on the left of the speaker shows the master volume all the time, no hold needed: full volume fills the whole half circle, half volume a quarter. An arrow above and below the speaker steps the volume by 5%. Tap or drag on the ring to set it. Tapping the speaker still silences, and holding it still opens the mixer.

**Settings as code, the </> button at the top of Settings.** It writes the look on stage (grid, lines, sounds, mix, tempo, the field) as one line you can share three ways: copy the code, copy a link that opens Battanboo with this look, or download it as a file. Paste a line (or drop a file) into the box and Apply opens it. Save keeps it on this device with a number (Battanboo look 001, 002…) in a row you can tap to open, so a change never overwrites one you already have; Forget removes one after a second tap. Nothing pasted is ever run as code.

**Room mode for the grid, and a speaker line.** The grid now has a **Room**: you sit in the middle, the top rows are in front of you and the bottom rows behind you, left and right as drawn. Farther and behind sounds softer, darker and wetter. (The old Room is now called **Stage**.) The Air pop-up and the cube show what you are hearing, with an ear for two speakers and a speaker for four: "2 speakers", "4 speakers", or "made for 4, you hear 2" when headphones or a Bluetooth box give only two. The grid itself still plays on two outputs; true four-speaker routing of grid notes comes later.
**Copy report, Email report and Clear marks show a green check** when tapped, so you can see it worked.
**The Performance sections list no longer stops with an error.** The Muted list could not open ("Can't find variable: controls", found by the iPad self-test). Fixed in the shared kit.

**The light-sound test is now a switch in the app.** The iPad's home-screen app has no address bar to type `?lite` into. In Soniscale's settings (the Field pane, below Limit) there is now **Light sound (a test for crackle)** with Normal and Light. Light switches off the heavy master smoothing, the Air grains and long reverbs together; it restarts the app and stays until you set it back to Normal. If the crunchy noise stops with Light on, we know it is one of those three.

**The error notice no longer cries wolf.** Resizing the window, turning an iPad or going full screen made Chrome report a harmless note that could open "Something went wrong"; it is ignored now, and the error notice stays quiet in audience view and the cinema view. A passing message no longer pushes away a note from the studio.

**The line under the grid runs all the way across.** On an iPad the score line ("Score 1 of 1 · Now: 49 bpm · Radar, clockwise + Square widening…") was held to about 416 px and cut off with "…" although the screen had room. It now uses the whole width, so a long line-up fits on one line. On a phone, where it is still too long, a tap opens it in full as before.

**A light-sound test for the iPad crackle.** Open Battanboo with `?lite` at the end of its address and the three heaviest steady jobs in the sound engine are switched off together: the smoothing on the master (no oversampling), the Air grains, and long reverbs (held to 2 seconds). A line at the top says the test is on. If the crackle stops, one of those three is the cause. Without `?lite`, nothing changes. The buffer test's note now uses the same line at the top.

**Everything Battanboo has to tell you now speaks from the same line at the top.** The small passing messages that sat in the top right corner, warnings (a controller disconnected, something refused), "The sound stopped" with Restart the sound, Reset and Report it, and the error screen (Reload, Report it, Keep going) all open as one line at the top centre, like the update notice; tap it for more, × to close. Report it opens the system check, ready to copy or email. Not shown in audience view or the cinema view.
